title: Panacea: Novel DNN Accelerator using Accuracy-Preserving Asymmetric Quantization and Energy-Saving Bit-Slice Sparsity
problem: Symmetric quantization introduces unacceptable accuracy loss for large-scale DNNs due to asymmetric activation distributions, but existing asymmetric quantization schemes produce many nonzero bit-slices that cannot be exploited by bit-slice GEMM accelerators designed for symmetric (zero-heavy) representations.
motivation: Bit-slice sparsity acceleration requires skippable zero slices, yet the nonzero-heavy output of asymmetric quantization wastes this opportunity, leaving a gap between accuracy and hardware efficiency in large DNN deployments.
method: Panacea introduces Asymmetrically-Quantized bit-Slice GEMM (AQS-GEMM), which compresses frequent nonzero slices generated by asymmetric quantization and skips their computation. Two algorithm-hardware co-optimization techniques increase slice-level sparsity: zero-point manipulation (adjusting quantization zero points to shift frequent values toward zero) and distribution-based bit-slicing (selecting bit-slices that maximize sparsity based on activation distribution). Panacea's dataflow is specialized for sparse/dense mixed workloads on tiled AQS-GEMM, with run-length encoding to maximize data reuse and minimize off-chip memory traffic.
key_novelty: AQS-GEMM: the first bit-slice GEMM formulation that compresses and skips nonzero slices produced by asymmetric quantization rather than only exploiting symmetric zero slices.
contributions: AQS-GEMM: asymmetrically-quantized bit-slice GEMM that skips compressed frequent nonzero slices
Zero-point manipulation algorithm to maximize slice-level sparsity in asymmetrically quantized activations
Distribution-based bit-slicing to further increase sparsity by choosing sparsity-maximizing bit-slice subsets
Panacea accelerator with specialized sparse/dense tiled dataflow achieving 1.97x energy and 1.88x throughput over Sibia on OPT-2.7B

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 1.97x energy efficiency over Sibia, 3.26x over SIMD on OPT-2.7B
metrics.speedup: 1.88x throughput over Sibia, 2.41x over SIMD on OPT-2.7B

limitations: The accuracy impact of zero-point manipulation and distribution-based bit-slicing for models beyond OPT-2.7B is not fully characterized in the abstract.
